solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fellow politicians going round boundaries of Atlas range

parts.note: CO is a prefix meaning fellow or joint, as in co-worker

indicators.note: the politicians' letters are placed around the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: MPs are Members of Parliament

indicators.note: the boundaries of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Fellow members of parliament are on a trip around the Atlas mountains of Morocco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Atlas range' reads as one mountain chain, but 'range' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Range and compass both mean scope or extent, as in the full compass of a voice.

clue.text: "Stick together" — something eg colonel may say on phone?

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer, often a colonel
here is what someone says announcing themselves on the phone

explanation.surface: An officer announces himself on the line with an order to stay united.
explanation.walkthrough: A commanding officer phoning would say 'CO here'.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to hold fast or stay united as a whole.

clue.text: Entertainer in Paris that's restricted by mother's resistance

indicators.note: the French word is hemmed in by the letters for mother's resistance

parts.note: ma's is a familiar form of mother's
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
que is French for that

explanation.surface: A performer in Paris is held back by his mother's opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is 'that is': QUE is restricted by MA'S R.
explanation.definitionFit: A masquer is a performer in a masque, a courtly entertainment, or anyone at a masquerade.

clue.text: A brave man disheartened about a Mycenaean king

parts.note: game means plucky or brave, as in game for anything

indicators.note: taking the heart out of a word leaves only its outer letters

parts.note: on means about or concerning, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: A courageous fellow loses heart over an ancient Greek ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was the legendary ruler of Mycenae who led the Greeks at Troy.

clue.text: Ride this ultimately — and go off heroin?

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of this

parts.note: to addle is to go off or turn rotten, as an egg does
horse is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A rider is told to finish the course and kick a drug habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A ride can mean an animal for riding, a mount, which is what this kind of horse is.

clue.text: Earnest South American touring eastern port

indicators.note: the South American pair travels round the port, so its letters enclose it

parts.note: US stands for American, as in US citizen
Rio de Janeiro is the famous Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A solemn South American is visiting a port in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' looks like one description, but its two abbreviations are split so the port sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest and serious are synonyms describing someone grave and sincere in manner.

clue.text: European leader banished from island? Heavens!

indicators.note: the letter is expelled from the island's name

parts.note: Skye is an island of the Scottish Hebrides

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cry of surprise as a European ruler is exiled from an island.
explanation.walkthrough: SKYE is a Scottish island; the heavens means the sky, the exclamation dressing it.
explanation.definitionFit: The heavens is a poetic term for the firmament overhead, so the expanse above the earth.

clue.text: Puzzle concerning rising press employee

parts.note: re means concerning, as in business letters

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a sub is a subeditor at a newspaper

explanation.surface: A conundrum about a newspaper worker getting promoted.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a picture puzzle in which symbols and images stand for words.

clue.text: Rejection of a bank arrangement primarily means independent paper folding

indicators.note: rejection is read as re-jection, throwing back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a giro is a bank transfer system, familiar in Britain

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of means

explanation.surface: A bank declining a payment primarily means an independent person must fold paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejection of' turns A GIRO into ORIGA.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of folding paper into decorative shapes.

clue.text: Walk purposefully over books in grating?

indicators.note: in a down entry the walking word sits over, above, the books

parts.note: to stride is to walk with long decisive steps
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: Someone marches over volumes on a metal grid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grating' looks like a noun, a grid, but it is the adjective, harsh-sounding.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident voice is harsh and loud, as jarring as a rasping noise.

clue.text: Management originally supplying musicians for a king in haste

indicators.note: the new letters stand in for the king's letter, replacing it

parts.note: haste means hurry, as in more haste less speed
R is short for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word supplying

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: A manager first supplied a band to a king who was in a rush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' signals substitution: SBAND replaces one R of HURRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Husbandry is careful management of resources, as in animal husbandry or good financial husbandry.

clue.text: Prickly shrub, one accommodated by Remus's brother

indicators.note: the numeral is housed inside the brother's name

parts.note: Brer, a dialect form of brother, is how Uncle Remus names the animals in his tales, as in Brer Rabbit
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A thorny bush, perhaps, housed by Romulus, brother of Remus in Roman legend.
explanation.walkthrough: Remus suggests Romulus, but this is Uncle Remus of the Joel Chandler Harris stories, whose 'brother' is BRER.
explanation.definitionFit: Brier, also spelt briar, is a thorny bush such as the wild rose.

clue.text: Most of message received about high-class cosmetic

indicators.note: the shortened word goes around the next letter
most of the word means its final letter is dropped

parts.note: Roger is radio-speak for message received
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: Part of a message about a smart make-up product has come through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops the last R of ROGER, leaving ROGE, which goes 'about' U.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouge is a red powder or cream applied to the cheeks as make-up.

clue.text: Many go ashore, united in this idyllic place

indicators.note: the letter for united is placed inside the word for many

parts.note: lots means many, as in lots of people
U is the abbreviation for united, as in Man U
to land is to go ashore from a ship

explanation.surface: A crowd disembarks together in a paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Odyssey, Odysseus's crew landed on the lotus-eaters' isle, which the surface evokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotus-land is a place of dreamy, contented ease, after the lotus-eaters of Greek myth.

clue.text: Star in Nepal travelling across certain mountains

indicators.note: the letters travel about and settle in a new order

explanation.surface: A celebrity is on a trip in the Himalayan kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Transalpine means on or crossing to the far side of the Alps, a particular mountain range.

clue.text: Hard finance can supply a Quebecois, perhaps

indicators.note: read as supply, meaning in a supple or bendy way, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Tough money can provide for someone from Quebec.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a verb, but it is read as an adverb from supple, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Quebec is Canada's French-speaking province, so its people are an example of French Canadians.

clue.text: Gave up being promiscuous?

definitions.meaning: to have given something up is to have deserted or relinquished it
an immoral, wanton person is described as unrestrained and dissolute

explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned is past tense of a verb for deserting, and also an adjective for wild, loose behaviour.

clue.text: Stupid to procced without the Marines?

parts.note: to go is to proceed; procced is a misspelling in the published clue
RM stands for the Royal Marines
less means without, as in a cup less its handle

explanation.surface: Is it foolish to advance without the Royal Marines?
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like an instruction to drop RM, but it is the word LESS in a plain charade.
explanation.definitionFit: Gormless is informal British for dim-witted and clueless.

clue.text: Rating part of Mass, calls back to cover front of altar

parts.note: the Ordinary is the unchanging part of the Catholic Mass

indicators.note: the reversed word covers, so contains, the next letter
back means the word for calls is read in reverse

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them

indicators.note: front of means the opening letter of altar

explanation.surface: A liturgical piece in which the names are recited over the altar's front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NAMES into SEMAN, which goes round the A of altar.
explanation.definitionFit: A rating is a non-commissioned sailor; an ordinary seaman is the lowest such rank in the Royal Navy.

clue.text: Lethargic porter dropping round at end of shift

indicators.note: dropping means one letter is let go from the porter's word

parts.note: a doorman is a porter at a building's entrance
O is round in shape

indicators.note: at end of takes the last letter of shift

explanation.surface: A tired doorkeeper finishes his shift with a round of drinks forgone.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormant means inactive or sleeping, as torpid and sluggish as a lethargic creature.

clue.text: Layman in a primeval city imbibing milky infusion …

indicators.note: the city drinks in, so contains, the infusion

parts.note: Ur is an ancient city of Mesopotamia
maté is a South American herbal tea, sometimes taken with milk

explanation.surface: A lay visitor in an ancient city sips a milky brew.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the surface to the next clue but plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A layman is a non-professional, and an amateur likewise does something without being an expert.

clue.text: … one in a box dispatched by public transport?

parts.note: sent means dispatched or posted
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Someone in a box is posted off by rail.
explanation.walkthrough: The box is a sentry box, the hut a guard stands in.
explanation.definitionFit: A guard on duty often stands in a small shelter called a sentry box.

clue.text: Like some rock male member initially explained in exam

parts.note: an arm is a limb, or member, of the body

indicators.note: the initial letter is put inside the word for exam

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of explained

explanation.surface: A man's limb first explained in a geology test, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmoreal means of or like marble, which is a kind of rock.

clue.text: Last letter from girl in borders of Oklahoma

indicators.note: the name is put inside the two border letters
the borders of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: Meg is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A final note from a girl living on the Oklahoma border.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Elizabethan navigator finally turned libertine

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of turned

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute, pleasure-seeking man

explanation.surface: A sixteenth-century seafarer ended up a debauchee.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis Drake was a sea captain who circumnavigated the globe under Queen Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Get up close to one, not early!

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, here from one

parts.note: late is the opposite of early

explanation.surface: Someone is told to rise near a certain hour but not too soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get up' reads as rising from bed; here it means to lift someone's spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: To get someone up can mean to excite or thrill them, much as to make them jubilant.

clue.text: In which properly dressed soldiers are lamenting breaking up

definitions.text: In which properly dressed soldiers are

indicators.note: breaking up the word shatters its letters, which are put together in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Smartly turned-out troops weep as they disband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed' is the drill sense: soldiers dress by lining up in straight ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops who are dressed on parade stand in straight lines, which is being in alignment.

clue.text: Diver from area to north of this country

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits above, north of, the second

parts.note: for a British newspaper this country is the UK

explanation.surface: A diver from a region north of Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The auk is a seabird that dives underwater for fish.

clue.text: Misfortune revealed by our education supplement, initially?

parts.note: the Times Educational Supplement is known by its initials, TES, which are the word set written back to front

explanation.surface: A bad turn shown up in The Times's own schools paper.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as an instruction, SET back, gives the clue's initials TES. 'our' because this is The Times, publisher of the supplement.
explanation.definitionFit: A setback is a reverse or piece of bad luck that hinders progress.

clue.text: Ageing English lord residing at first in cathedral city

indicators.note: these letters go inside the name of the city

parts.note: Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of residing

explanation.surface: An English peer of advancing years lives in a cathedral town.
explanation.walkthrough: ELY is a city in eastern England with a famous cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly describes someone getting on in years, so growing old.
